label: copy-phase input r, mid-recall (recall_idx 2-4) in long sequences, before certain outputs
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is the letter r (100% of activations). It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on any other input token. It is concentrated mid-recall: recall_idx 3 holds 71% of mass and 2-4 hold 97%; t=12 in L=9 sequences holds 52%. Rate and magnitude grow with L (L=9 has 66% of mass, L<=5 almost none). The top activations are all r at orig(2) being fed back at recall_idx 3 of an L=9 sequence. Activation also depends on the token being output next: r, u, f, s, n, d, i, p, h favor firing, while y, x, l, a, q, j mostly suppress it. Even in the best context it fires on only a fraction of eligible steps (L=9, recall 3, favored outputs: ~79% precision), so some unexplained modulation remains. Copy-phase r at recall 2-4 covers 97% of mass with only 6% precision; adding the output-token set and L>=7 brings dev F1 to 0.41 with mass recall 0.82.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: r, -, v, g, c, u; least: j, d, h, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: r, f, u, s, p, n; least: z, 3, -, q); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, t=12, L=9 & t=13.
